title: The gate's own host contention refuses innocent work; bound it
description:
Two of cy2's occurrences landed today, and both were refused under package-level contention rather than any fault of the tick. The deeper issue is that NOTHING BOUNDS WHAT ELSE RUNS while the gate runs.

The gate is the one runner that can block every tick. It runs 'go test -short -parallel 12 ./...' on whatever host happens to be free, alongside whatever else that host is doing — other workers, other agents, another gate, and on 2026-09-19 four runaway busy-loops the orchestrator itself left behind. internal/reconcile's cost is process spawning, so its wall time swings from ~200s idle to 845s under load, and the wall-clock-sensitive tests fire somewhere in between.

cy2 is about making those tests robust, which is right and is the real fix. This tick is the other half: the gate should not be a coin flip on host weather.

Options worth weighing, not a prescription:
- Serialise gates per host. Two gates at -parallel 12 on a 10-core machine is 24 test processes plus their forks; nothing prevents that today.
- Refuse to START a gate above a load threshold, and say so, rather than running one that will produce an untrustworthy verdict.
- Report the host's load alongside the gate evidence, so a refusal can be read against the conditions it was produced in. Cheap, and it would have answered today's question immediately instead of costing an hour.
- Consider whether the gate belongs on the same host as the workers at all.

The third option is the cheapest and probably first: a verdict with no record of the conditions cannot be argued with.

Related: cy2 (the tests themselves), and the Makefile's GOTEST_PARALLEL note, which already says returns stop at 12 'while host load, and so the risk on the one wall-clock-sensitive test, only grows past it' — the risk was named and left unbounded.
acceptance_criteria: Gate evidence records the host conditions the verdict was produced under, and concurrent gate runs on one host are bounded or refused with a stated reason
